record.paper_title: Geodesic Nets: Some Examples and Open Problems
record.context_brief: fixed boundary tuple with unbounded planar nets
record.original_question: Does there exist an integer N0 and a fixed N0-tuple S of points in the Euclidean plane such that, for every integer N at least 1, there is a finite connected embedded geodesic net whose set of unbalanced vertices is exactly S and whose number of balanced vertices is greater than N? Moreover, does the collection of such N0-tuples contain a subset of (R^2)^N0 of positive Lebesgue measure, or even a nonempty open subset?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.3.1. 1. There exist N0 and an N0 -tuple S such that for each N there exists a geodesic net with S being its set of unbalanced vertices and the number of balanced vertices greater than N . 2. Furthermore, there exist not merely one such N0 -tuple S but a subset of (R2 )N0 of positive measure (or even a non-empty open subset) of such N0 -tuples.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A finite connected embedded geodesic net in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ is a finite connected graph embedded in $\mathbb{R}^2$ such that every edge is a straight line segment (a geodesic) and the edges meet only at their common vertices. A vertex $v$ of such a net is called balanced if the sum of the unit tangent vectors along the edges incident to $v$, pointing away from $v$, equals the zero vector; otherwise $v$ is called unbalanced.

Question:
(a) Does there exist a positive integer $N_0$ and a fixed $N_0$-tuple $S = (p_1,\dots,p_{N_0}) \in (\mathbb{R}^2)^{N_0}$ such that, for every integer $N \geq 1$, there exists a finite connected embedded geodesic net in $\mathbb{R}^2$ whose set of unbalanced vertices equals $\{p_1,\dots,p_{N_0}\}$ and whose number of balanced vertices exceeds $N$?

(b) If so, does the set of $N_0$-tuples $S \in (\mathbb{R}^2)^{N_0}$ having the property in (a) contain a subset of positive Lebesgue measure in $(\mathbb{R}^2)^{N_0}$, or even a nonempty open subset?
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture appears to still be open. Recent work (2024–2025) makes partial progress by constructing planar geodesic nets with four unbalanced (boundary) vertices and an increasing number of balanced vertices (raising the known maximum from 16 to 25), but does not produce an unbounded family for a fixed boundary tuple, nor establish positive-measure/open sets of such tuples. For three unbalanced vertices it is known that at most one balanced vertex can occur, so the conjecture is necessarily about $N_0 \geq 4$.

status_evidence.title: Towards Constructing Geodesic Nets with Four Boundary Vertices and an Increasing Number of Balanced Vertices
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs a geodesic net in the plane with four boundary vertices and 25 balanced vertices, improving the previous maximum of 16.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress: a construction with four unbalanced vertices and 25 balanced vertices, but no unbounded family for a fixed boundary tuple.

status_evidence.title: Geodesic nets with three boundary vertices
status_evidence.snippet: A geodesic net in the plane with three unbalanced vertices has at most one balanced vertex.
status_evidence.claim: For three unbalanced vertices the number of balanced vertices is bounded by 1, so the conjecture requires N0 >= 4.

status_evidence.title: Geodesic Nets: Some Examples and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: States the conjecture about existence of an N0-tuple S with unbounded numbers of balanced vertices, and asks whether the set of such tuples has positive measure or contains an open set.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is stated as an open problem.
